outcome: Relative abundances of gut microbial genera (Enterococcus, Staphylococcus, Bacteroides, Parabacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Escherichia, Streptococcus)
cohort: The study included 13 neonates with congenital heart disease and 30 healthy control neonates.
finding: Neonates with CHD exhibited an intestinal core microbiota dominated by Enterococcus and Staphylococcus, with lower abundances of Bacteroides, Parabacteroides, Bifidobacterium, and Escherichia compared to healthy controls, and oxygen saturation significantly impacted microbiota composition.
mod_finding: Among CHD patients, vaginal delivery was associated with lower fractions of Bacteroides and Bifidobacterium compared to healthy controls, while these genera were entirely absent in CHD neonates born by cesarean section.
